findings.body: The browser accepts and submits the attachment instead of rejecting it with the configured limit, so the upload fails later on the server; attachments on sites allowing more than 10 MB are also rejected prematurely.
findings.failure_mode: Client and server upload validation disagree, producing late upload failures or rejecting valid attachments.
findings.impact: The browser accepts and submits the attachment instead of rejecting it with the configured limit, so the upload fails later on the server; attachments on sites allowing more than 10 MB are also rejected prematurely.
findings.root_cause: A universal 10 MB literal replaced the type-specific site setting used by client validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Select the limit by upload type, using max_attachment_size_kb for attachments while applying the intended source-image limit only to images.
findings.title: Client-side validation ignores the configured attachment limit
findings.trigger: A non-image attachment is selected while max_attachment_size_kb is below 10240, such as a 5 MB attachment on a site configured for a 3 MB limit.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 182 shows `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. For attachments, this ignores max_attachment_size_kb setting. If max_attachment_size_kb < 10240, client accepts files server will reject; if > 10240, client rejects valid files. Trigger and impact are realistic.

findings.body: Ruby resolves the later definition and raises ArgumentError for the five-argument call, so emoji resizing jobs abort and oversized emoji are not reduced.
findings.failure_mode: A previously valid background-job execution path fails before invoking the image processor.
findings.impact: Ruby resolves the later definition and raises ArgumentError for the five-argument call, so emoji resizing jobs abort and oversized emoji are not reduced.
findings.root_cause: Ruby method overloading was attempted by defining downsize twice; the later four-argument definition replaces the earlier five-argument definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one downsize method that supports the legacy width/height call shape and the new geometry-string shape, or update every caller before removing the old signature.
findings.title: The new downsize overload breaks emoji resizing jobs
findings.trigger: The existing ResizeEmoji job calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts) with five arguments.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows two `def self.downsize` methods at lines 145-147 and 149-151. Ruby replaces the first with the second (4-arg signature becomes 3-arg). ResizeEmoji job at line 14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args, which will raise ArgumentError against the 3-arg definition.

raw_findings.body: The user-facing dialog claims the maximum is 10240 KB even though the request was rejected at another limit, making the upload limit and corrective action misleading.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error handling reports a limit that does not match the component that rejected the request.
raw_findings.impact: The user-facing dialog claims the maximum is 10240 KB even though the request was rejected at another limit, making the upload limit and corrective action misleading.
raw_findings.root_cause: The configured maximum was replaced with a hard-coded display value without synchronizing the proxy limit or the error source.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the configured image limit or an error value supplied by the server/proxy instead of an unconditional 10240 KB value.
raw_findings.title: 413 errors display an incorrect maximum size
raw_findings.trigger: The web server or proxy returns HTTP 413 at a configured limit different from 10 MB, such as the default 3072 KB image setting documented for proxy configuration.

raw_findings.body: The URL download is rejected before the controller can downsize the image, while an equivalent multipart upload can follow the configured limit; the rescued nil can then cause the upload path to fail instead of processing the image.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The URL API path has a lower and inconsistent acceptance limit than the normal upload path.
raw_findings.impact: The URL download is rejected before the controller can downsize the image, while an equivalent multipart upload can follow the configured limit; the rescued nil can then cause the upload path to fail instead of processing the image.
raw_findings.root_cause: The API download limit was changed from the site setting to an unconditional 10 MB cap.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a single, explicitly defined source-size policy derived from the site configuration for URL and multipart uploads, and preserve the configured limit when it permits larger images.
raw_findings.title: API URL uploads are capped at 10 MB independently of the configured image limit
raw_findings.trigger: An API client uploads an image by URL that is larger than 10 MB but within a site-configured max_image_size_kb of more than 10240, or an unlimited setting.

raw_findings.body: OptimizedImage selects its non-animated conversion path because it tests the temporary path suffix, and that path reads only frame 0, so the stored upload becomes a static image.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The preprocessing step silently changes animated image data into a single-frame image.
raw_findings.impact: OptimizedImage selects its non-animated conversion path because it tests the temporary path suffix, and that path reads only frame 0, so the stored upload becomes a static image.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new caller requests animation preservation but supplies a temporary path to dispatch logic that detects GIFs only from the source-path extension.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the original filename or an explicit image format/animation flag into the optimizer and select the animated instructions based on the actual GIF content rather than the temporary path suffix.
raw_findings.title: Oversized animated GIF uploads lose their animation during downsizing
raw_findings.trigger: An oversized animated GIF is uploaded through the multipart path while allow_animated_thumbnails is true; the Rack temporary file path does not retain the original .GIF filename suffix.

finding.title: Oversized animated GIF uploads lose their animation during downsizing
finding.trigger: An oversized animated GIF is uploaded through the multipart path while allow_animated_thumbnails is true; the Rack temporary file path does not retain the original .GIF filename suffix.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch line 67 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` where tempfile.path is a Rack temp path without .GIF extension. Line 155 shows animation detection uses `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Animated GIFs uploaded via multipart will have temp paths like /tmp/RackMultipart..., failing the regex and losing animation.
